subject: Post-call recap + target $/1M tokens benchmarking (Redwood vs OpenAI/Anthropic)
messages:

Subject: Post-call recap + target $/1M tokens benchmarking (Redwood vs OpenAI/Anthropic)

Hi Jordan —

Thanks for your time earlier. Quick recap and next steps from our discovery:

1) Current usage and ramp
- Today: ~120M tokens/month across internal pilot (mix of completions + embeddings)
- Target ramp: 300-500M tokens/month over the next 6-9 months if pilot scales as expected
- Peak: ~10-12M tokens/day during busiest hours

2) Requirements we heard
- Consistent latency for chat flows (~<200ms p50 token latency)
- Ability to pin model variants and fallback to cheaper open-models during heavy load
- Strong cost predictability (looking to avoid surprise overages)

3) Pricing ask from your side
- You mentioned a target price band and asked for benchmarking vs OpenAI/Anthropic and common open-model hosts - specifically target $/1M tokens that would make sense for your 300-500M run rate.

4) Attachments & next steps
- Attached: redwood_vs_hosts_token_pricing.xlsx (quick benchmarking + 3 pricing scenarios: Hosted, Dedicated reserved, Private) and acme_ramp_forecast.csv (we populated the ramp numbers you shared).
- Action items: please confirm the expected monthly volume bands and desired target price per 1M tokens; we’ll send a short pricing options email (hosted vs dedicated) and propose a follow-up to review the economics.

Would Wednesday 8/4 at 10am PT work for a short follow-up to run through the scenarios?

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Sales Lead, Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com
Redwood Inference

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Ellis <jordan.ellis@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@acme.com>
Date: 2027-08-01T15:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + target $/1M tokens benchmarking (Redwood vs OpenAI/Anthropic)

Jordan -

Great, thanks for the clarity. Attached spreadsheet has three practical scenarios and a high-level benchmarking vs OpenAI/Anthropic and common open-model hosts. Quick summary tailored to the 300-500M target band:

- Hosted API (no commit): $15 / 1M tokens (standard tier). Pros: fastest time-to-value, predictable dev experience, no infra ops. Cons: higher unit cost unless you accept a commit.
- Dedicated (reserved capacity, 12-month commit): $9 / 1M tokens for volumes in the 300-500M/month band. This assumes a 12-month commit and a standard SLA. We can do stepped pricing for first 3 months to reduce ramp exposure.
- Private (customer-managed infra or VPC): equivalent unit-rate can be ~$6-7 / 1M tokens (licensing + infra) but requires integration and you own infra ops; good for long-term cost optimization if you want full control.

Benchmarking (approximate market comparators):
- OpenAI: ~ $18-22 / 1M (depends on model family and rate limits)
- Anthropic: ~ $16-20 / 1M (model-dependent)
- Hosted open-model providers (self-hosting marketplaces / some hosts): ~ $10-14 / 1M depending on model and infra efficiency

So for your $8-12 /1M target: we can hit that in a Dedicated reserved model at ~$9 / 1M with a 12-month commit. If you need sub-12-month flexibility we can explore a ramped commit that starts at a slightly higher unit cost for months 1-3 and steps to $9 once volume stabilizes.

Unit economics notes (high level):
- Token mix matters - embeddings vs generation have different effective costs (embeddings cheaper per token in our benchmarking).
- Continuously batching and prefix/KV caching we apply reduces effective per-token cost by 10-25% for repeatable prompts; we’ll share recommendations in the spreadsheet.

Next steps
1) I’ll open a draft pricing option email (hosted vs dedicated) and share a short one-pager for your procurement team ahead of 8/4.
2) If 9/1 12-month commit meets your procurement needs we can price-match the dedicated scenario in a draft SOW / order form.
3) Please confirm if the $9 / 1M dedicated target (with a 12-month commit) is acceptable to start procurement conversations.

Link to quick benchmarking sheet: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/ACME-2027-045

See the attached for the scenarios (redwood_vs_hosts_token_pricing.xlsx). I’ll include Neha on the 8/4 call to talk through the quant/technical pieces.

Thanks,
Vanessa

Attachments: redwood_vs_hosts_token_pricing.xlsx (spreadsheet, 62KB)
